question: Why is one blank double_faced_token category C while ten blank double_faced_token records are category D?
summary: Classification is reproducible from type_line token detection, not an ad hoc exception.

categoryCRecord.whyCategoryC: typeLine is 'Card // Card' — does NOT match /\bToken\b/ or /\bEmblem\b/ or /\bVanguard\b/. Layout alone does not force category D. Blank rules text on a non-token Card-type double-faced punchcard is a legitimate Magic oracle identity with zero L2 actions.
categoryCRecord.classifierFunction: isNonCardTypeLine(typeLine) returns false; isLegitimateBlankMagicCard returns true

categoryDRecords.rule: typeLine contains 'Token' (Token Creature, Token Legendary Creature, etc.) => D even when oracle text is blank

representativeExamples.typeLine: Token Legendary Creature — Wolf // Token Creature — Saproling
Token Creature — Zombie // Token Creature — Zombie

categoryDRecords.note: All 10 D-category blank double_faced_token records have Token in typeLine. The single C record is the only blank DFT with Card // Card typing.

reproducibility.explicitImprovementOptional: Future classifier versions may emit reason code 'blank_double_faced_token_card_type' vs 'blank_double_faced_token_token_type_line' for audit clarity without changing counts.
